# Substrate University — Division charters for the Poly IA commission

**Governing decision:** the owner's current instruction assigns **Division Infinity to IX** and opens **VII and VIII as research charters**. This is a present constitutional decision. Earlier prohibitions on assigning VII/VIII, preserving an unnumbered Infinity overlay or keeping IX separate are historical source obligations with explicit supersession entries in the reconciliation system.

The names and boundaries of I–VI below are taken from the pinned canonical `sources/repos/abedkadaancom/src/content/registry.ts`. Existing topics, definitions, books, source links and computational contracts remain canonical. VII and VIII are opportunities to investigate and develop disciplines; the provisional titles below do not claim that the new fields are already established.

## DC-01. Common charter of every division

Every division maintains a versioned research object, terminology, source inventory, prerequisites, admitted operations, evidence rules, negative examples, curriculum and frontier. It registers how its objects map to the shared kernel without forcing its meanings into another division's vocabulary. Its conclusions distinguish established mathematics, house constructions, conjectures, measured results and authored presentation.

Each scientific unit must answer: What objects are admitted? Which transformations are defined? Under which assumptions? What is preserved or lost? What does a refusal mean? What evidence supports each claim? Which related questions remain unanswered? Its computational package and its teaching unit may have different maturity levels; both remain inspectable.

Shared state, packaging, source custody, tool contracts, verification, observability and guidance are University-wide infrastructure. No division owns the common harness or can relax its evidence rules. A cross-division project receives one source-linked record with several division views, rather than copied definitions that quietly diverge.

## DC-02. The adopted division map

| Division | Canonical or provisional title | Primary research objects | Poly IA obligation |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | Foundations of Computation | Transition systems, automata, grammars, admissibility, equivalence and computational cost | Ground machine behavior and distinguish a legal expression from a realizable computation |
| II | Relational and Generative Mathematics | Alphabets, folds, generative grammars, alphabet towers and constructive admission | Define and verify generation, promotion, expansion and cross-structure relations |
| III | Programmable Computational Languages | Typed languages, parsers, compilers, PURL/SEURL and addressable forms | Make machine-operable resources explicit, typed and source-linked |
| IV | Geometry, Physics, and Representation | Maps, images, kernels, charts, cameras, geometry and observational representations | Track transformations, domains, coordinate systems, losses and empirical interpretation |
| V | Acoustic and Generative Sciences | Signals, pitch, tuning, spectra, phase, synthesis and phonogrammatic forms | Separate signal computation, linguistic interpretation and perceptual or physical claims |
| VI | Computational Worlds and Emergence | Automata, procedural worlds, agent grammars, environments and world models | Build reproducible simulations and test claims about their behavior |
| VII | **Constructive Synthesis and Executable Forms — provisional** | Certified assemblies of operators, grammars and packages | Investigate when a specification can construct a useful executable object with a checkable derivation |
| VIII | **Experimental Evolution and Knowledge Continuity — provisional** | Versioned research systems, evidence transitions and improvement policies | Investigate how systems improve while preserving justified knowledge and traceable history |
| IX / ∞ | **Division Infinity — Calculus of Entangled Forms** | Typed form towers, n-ary entanglements, contextual strands and relation reification | Develop the inherited CEF/NEC/EFC research with explicit semantics and witnesses |

The existing six-division source has 62 registered topics, distributed 10/10/10/12/10/10. This is a pinned inventory fact, not a permanent ceiling. The commission's source-coverage report must count and resolve the actual pinned entries independently. The charters extend research responsibilities without rewriting the preserved source snapshot.

## DC-03. I–VI: continuity and scientific obligations

### I — Foundations of Computation

Preserve transition systems, graph theory, finite automata, equivalence classes, operational grammar, admissibility, numerical grammars, perturbation, substrate theory and complexity. The foundational obligation is to state both syntax and operational semantics, then test the boundary between membership, executability and cost.

The division must produce state/transition contracts for the commission and domain machines; meaningful negative tests; declared equality relations; complexity profiles with input and machine models; and curricula relating conventional computation theory to the inherited CGT and Grammar in Numbers sources. It must not identify `O(1)` lookup with free ingestion or output, or confuse numeral encoding with arithmetic value.

### II — Relational and Generative Mathematics

Preserve alphabets/words, generative grammars, recursive folds, Plicastratum, alphabet towers, modal/cyclic forms, relational generativity, constructive admission, Ingrammatica and compositional forms. The division studies which patterns can become reusable letters and what their promotion preserves.

Required results include certified expansion maps, namespaced closure properties, typed relation composition, a documented role for negative grammars and reproducible grammar-learning experiments. Compare promoted libraries against unpromoted baselines. A shorter representation alone is not proof of faster execution or deeper semantics.

### III — Programmable Computational Languages

Preserve URI grammar, typed machines, symbolic composition, types as admissibility, grammars as programs, compilation, Matrix Loom, PURL, SEURL and addressable forms. Addresses must resolve versioned context and operations. Read access remains observational; effectful operations require explicit commands.

Required outputs include typed grammars and AST/IR boundaries, source positions, API/protocol schemas, versioned SDK contracts, capability discovery and refusal behavior. A compiler must preserve the specified semantics through lowering and optimization. A parser, an interpreter and a target virtual machine remain distinct components. The live state service is the first operational application of this charter.

### IV — Geometry, Physics, and Representation

Preserve image/kernel, rank-nullity, Imagistratum, projective cameras, spatial tensors, topology, curvature, chart correspondences, celestial geometry, computational photography, rendering mathematics and invisible sensing. Astra integration belongs here jointly with I, III and VI.

Every transformation names its source/target spaces, coordinate conventions, units, near-plane or singularity behavior and information loss. Linear statements require linear assumptions. Simulated or authored geometry retains that label. A graph display's distance is not semantic distance unless an independently specified mapping establishes that interpretation.

### V — Acoustic and Generative Sciences

Preserve sound/signals, pitch/frequency, interval geometry, tuning, Fourier methods, phase, synthesis, time-frequency analysis, generative composition and Phonogrammatica. Signal transforms and finite grammars can generate sound without LLM inference.

Required outputs include sampling and reconstruction assumptions, bounded audio generation, reproducible phase/time models, mapping contracts for sonification and source-linked phonetic/linguistic adapters. Mathematical interval ratios, measured acoustic frequencies and listener perception are separate quantities. A playable waveform is evidence of software generation, not a clinical or perceptual result.

### VI — Computational Worlds and Emergence

Preserve cellular automata, World Loom, procedural environments, agent grammars, maps/navigation, BORNE, simulated populations, world models, GLM/LGM and HOMELESS/Dark. These applications consume shared semantics; they do not define all of Poly IA.

Required outputs include stateful simulation contracts, fixed or otherwise explicitly modeled clocks, seeded generation, world-state checkpoints and intervention experiments. An emergent pattern must be compared with controls and parameter sensitivity. Claims about people, biology or physical causation require evidence beyond the simulation. TREE's structural tree, coupling graph, render DAG and physics model remain distinct.

## DC-04. VII — Open charter in constructive synthesis

**Provisional title:** Constructive Synthesis and Executable Forms. **Status:** authorized research charter; title and boundaries remain revisable through recorded decisions.

**Object of study.** A specification and an available typed operator library, together with the derivations by which a candidate program, protocol, data structure, grammar, model or package is constructed. Its central question is when the construction is useful, explainable and checkable under explicit resource bounds.

**Initial questions.** Which source patterns can be promoted to reusable operators without changing refusal or effect semantics? When does library growth reduce search cost, and when does it merely enlarge the branching factor? Which cross-domain correspondences support executable reuse rather than analogy alone? What information must a package carry to remain reconstructible outside the environment that generated it?

**Methods.** Typed term enumeration; constraint propagation; syntax-guided synthesis; partial evaluation; rewrite systems; macro learning; finite-state and grammar-based generation; exact and differential verification. Established methods must remain cited as such. The new research contribution must be stated as a specific algorithm, contract, empirical result or composition—not as the mere existence of these methods together.

**First research productions.** A formally specified grammar-letter package; a synthesizer that composes at least one genuinely multi-input operation; a package generator that emits interfaces, source references, tests and evidence; and an explanation generator that realizes the same mathematical derivation in multiple registered presentation styles without LLM inference. Benchmark against fixed libraries and direct handwritten methods.

**Acceptance.** Every generated output has a construction trace and source versions. Generated code is examined or verified under its admitted target profile before execution. Record success rate, size, runtime and search cost against the baseline. Include unsatisfiable specifications, ambiguous interpretations and resource-limited searches. A failure to synthesize is not a proof of impossibility.

**Boundary.** Division II owns foundational alphabet/fold questions; III owns language/compilation interfaces. VII studies constructive assembly and the costs and guarantees of synthesis across them. Packaging services remain common infrastructure even though VII researches how packages can be generated.

## DC-05. VIII — Open charter in evidence-governed evolution

**Provisional title:** Experimental Evolution and Knowledge Continuity. **Status:** authorized research charter; its name is not a claim of an already established discipline.

**Object of study.** A research system's changing rules, code, representations, sources and evidence over time. Its central question is how the system can improve while retaining the ability to explain, reproduce and, where defined, reverse prior decisions.

**Initial questions.** Which improvement policies avoid overfitting to reused witnesses? When do changes preserve a package's semantic contracts? How should invalidated assumptions propagate through dependent claims? What is the smallest checkpoint sufficient to reconstruct a research decision? Can a learned scheduling policy improve discovery yield under the same resource envelope without corrupting evidential independence?

**Methods.** Versioned experimental design; baseline and ablation studies; dependency/impact analysis; preregistered criteria; held-out witnesses; deterministic event replay; reproducibility studies; migration equivalence checks; and bounded scheduling optimization. A novel checkpoint structure needs a measured benefit over ordinary event sourcing and content-addressed storage before a novelty claim.

**First research productions.** An improvement-epoch protocol; a comparison report showing a candidate and predecessor under the same conditions; a demonstrable invalidation cascade from a corrected source claim; a replay/reproduction distinction with real receipts; and an evaluation of scheduling policies under fixed cost limits.

**Acceptance.** The predecessor remains available. Changed outputs and dependent claims identify their old and new versions. The candidate cannot become active because it generated its own favorable score. A failed migration or inconclusive comparison stays inactive. Rollback states which data and external effects can actually be reversed; compensating actions are labeled separately.

**Boundary.** The shared harness serves every division. VIII investigates its scientific properties and improvement policies; it cannot make every ordinary logging task into a separate scientific discovery. It works with VII on synthesis candidates and IX on evidence-bearing relation changes.

## DC-06. IX — Infinity and the calculus of forms

**Adopted placement:** IX. **Inherited research names:** Calculus of Entangled Forms (CEF), Nomenclatural Entanglement Calculus (NEC), Entangled Form Complex (EFC). The source's earlier placement remains preserved as history.

The division studies typed transformations and relations among forms without collapsing byte representations, linguistic senses, mathematical objects, programs and empirical referents. It maintains the expression/interpretation distinction, arbitrary finite input/output arity, ordered role ports, multiple evidence strands, form towers, fibers, losses and relation reification.

Its first obligations are exact representation fidelity; contextual typed hyperedge admission; genuinely multi-input composition; independent strand statuses; nonunique inverse handling; and the refusal of causal or semantic claims inferred from encoding similarity alone. Later work studies invariance under recoding, useful topologies/lattices when their axioms hold, higher-order composition and corpus-wide discovery.

Each project states what “infinity” denotes: extensibility, arbitrarily long finite derivations, a mathematical limit or an explicitly defined infinite object. Every actual execution has a finite budget. The finite-registry closure theorem does not solve an expanding open-world search.

## DC-07. Knot, language bridges and publication boundaries

Division Knot/DK0 is retained as a cross-cutting relational view; it is not assigned VII or VIII by implication. The source's “Division Not” wording is preserved with its resolution status. Neither charter authorizes inventing a missing foundational text.

The public University repository has its own publication rules and scope. Poly IA preserves and studies all supplied language and continuity material in the complete research corpus, including sources outside that public site's current subject policy. Publishing those materials into the public University requires an explicit compatible policy decision; preserving them in Poly IA requires no such deletion or omission. The current owner's division decision changes the division mandate, not every unrelated publication rule.

## DC-08. Books and curriculum are first-class productions

The complete corpus includes published books, source manuscripts, generated volumes, composition code and historical specimen labels. All are incorporated. Original publication status remains metadata so that a generated volume is not mislabeled a published monograph, and no item is discarded because of that status.

Each book receives a stable source ID, edition, digest, chapter/section structure, extractable positions and a mapping to topics, terms and experiments. A chapter that teaches a construction must link to its assumptions and executable or scholarly verification where available. A newly generated course or book is versioned output with a declared editorial process; it does not silently replace its sources.
